verdict.line: Yorick out-trades and out-kills you through the early levels off Q (Last Rites) poke and the Mourning Mist-into-Dark Procession wall combo, but you flip the matchup to a 59% head-to-head win rate over 117 games once Q (Siphoning Strike) stacks and core items come online.

brief.thesis: Yorick holds lane advantage and solo-kill advantage because Q (Last Rites) gives him a free damage-and-heal poke and his E (Mourning Mist) into W (Dark Procession) combo turns any melee commit into a kill box, but Nasus's stacking Q and the Fury of the Sands health-drain ultimate convert that early disadvantage into the stronger champion by mid-to-late game. This is a lane-to-survive, game-to-win matchup, not an even fight at any single point in time.

theirWindow.when: after his E lands a mark on you
theirWindow.what: He is about to drop W (Dark Procession) behind or beside you to wall you against himself and free-hit with Q resets. Do not stand still trading; walk out of the mark radius immediately instead of contesting the trade.

yourWindow.when: both his E and W are on cooldown
yourWindow.what: He has no way to anchor you in place, so this is your safe window to walk up and melee the wave with Q (Siphoning Strike) or step in for a real trade, since Wither punishes any attempt he makes to walk back into range.

start.why: Runs at 56.3% win over 128 games and 76.7% pick; the flat damage block and regen absorb Yorick's Q (Last Rites) poke so he can't zone you off farm before stacks matter.

boots.why: 62.2% win over 90 games and the majority pick; the cooldown reduction tightens your Q (Siphoning Strike) and W (Wither) cycle, which matters more than the raw armor from Plated Steelcaps once you're farming through his combo instead of brawling it.

core.why: Backbone of the 52.9% win path; the damage spike is what turns your stacked Q into real trading power once lane calms down.
Shared across both top build paths; the cooldown reduction and armor let you spam E (Spirit Fire) for armor shred while tanking Yorick's autos.
Completes the top core path (52.9% win, 16.8% pick); stacks with Soul Eater lifesteal to win extended skirmishes he tries to force.

runes.keystoneWhy: The run-50%, pick-51.5% page; the healing and movement speed on hit let you step into farm range for Q stacks and step back out before his E-W wall combo locks you down, which matters far more into Yorick than a flat damage keystone.

summoners.why: Ghost+Teleport is both the most-picked (47.2%) and highest-winning (61%) combo in this matchup; Ghost lets you close or break off from his Mourning Mist slow without burning Flash, and Teleport is your actual win condition since a stacked Q threatens side lanes once you've lost early lane tempo.

playing.title: Farm Q, don't force fights
playing.detail: Prioritize Siphoning Strike last-hits over trades through the early levels; every kill is a permanent stack, and OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to focus stacking over contesting Yorick's early strength.

playing.title: Treat a dropped wall as a kill box
playing.detail: The moment his E (Mourning Mist) mark lands, assume W (Dark Procession) is coming to wall you in with him. Walk away from the mark radius rather than trading inside it.

playing.title: Poke with Spirit Fire from range
playing.detail: E (Spirit Fire) has 650 range versus his melee Q; drop it on the wave or on him preemptively to shred armor and chip damage without entering the range where his combo can trap you.

playing.title: Save Wither for his commits
playing.detail: Hold W (Wither) until he overextends or walls you in, then use the Movement and Attack Speed deceleration to either walk out safely or punish the follow-up since he can no longer kite or stick.

playing.title: Watch his graves, not just his HP
playing.detail: His passive raises Mist Walkers from graves Q digs; a Yorick who's been digging graves uncontested has more backup in the next fight, so punish lane states where he hasn't.

playing.title: Time R around your stack count
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands' health drain scales harder the more Q stacks you've banked; save it for turning a 1v1 or sieging a turret once your stacks make the trade one-sided.

playing.title: Split-push once stacked
playing.detail: Since you're losing the lane-kill race early, your real win condition is threatening side lanes with Teleport once Q stacks make you a bigger problem than the lane he's winning.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, runes, boots, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures come from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (9,000 Nasus games overall, 117 in this exact matchup); the lane-phase reasoning, power-spike timing, and trade patterns are my own read of the kit, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Focus on farming with [Q] to gain stacks. It is vital that you do not get caught inside Yorick’s (E)-(W) combo when engaging him.
